LESSON: SIGN READING 14.4.1 CLASS READER: FEATURES OF STYLE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Sign Reading 14.4.1 Class reader: Features of style
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 14.4.1 Class reader: Features of style, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we convey a message more effectively? 2. Why do we use similes and metaphors?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 14.4.1 Class reader: Features of style together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learners develop negotiation skills as they hold a discussion on instances in real life where dialogues, similes, and

metaphors can be used.

● Learning to learn: Learners develop the skill of organising own work as they record and share videos role playing selected dialogues.

Values:
● Respect: is enhanced as learners help each other during role-play of selected dialogues.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates features of style in the study of class readers to the learning of readers in Kiswahili.
